Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital identity systems and credentials. 30 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: National ID: centralized ABIS biometric registry, data localized (previously stored offshore, resolved). eCRVS: HERA software (WCC, 2023), 1.2M records, AWS cloud hosted. Multiple electronic databases exist but fragmented across ministries; not a single unified system.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The 2023 World Bank diagnostic (single source) described fragmented but electronic databases (ABIS + eCRVS), supporting Value Code 2 at the time. However, on 29-30 June 2026 Gambia went live with the new National Identity Management System (NIMS/GAM ID), corroborated by five independent Gambian and trade-press outlets, which established a single unified, fully electronic National Identity Register hosted at a new purpose-built National Data Centre (Abuko), with biometric enrolment, chip-based credentials and real-time verification replacing the old fragmented records. This now meets the 'Digital' definition (Value Code 3); the original score is outdated given the June 2026 system launch.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: 831,747 national ID card holders against total population of ~2.42M (~34% total, ~60% of adults 18+). eCRVS birth registration covers ~50% (1.2M). Strategy target: 75% registered in National Biometric ID. Mass enrollment 2022-2023: 1,167,460 (all ages) issued health insurance/birth cert via eCRVS. Coverage partial; World Bank diagnostic notes 'Low coverage (63%+)' for ID.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed at Value Code 2 (20-49%): 831,747 old national ID card holders against the 2024 GBOS census population of 2,422,712 (~34%) is the most recent verifiable figure for issued ID credentials, corroborated by the 2024 GBOS census and World Bank/Biometric Update reporting on the separate ~54% eCRVS birth-registration coverage. Note this figure is about to be superseded: Gambia's old ID system is being replaced by the new NIMS/GAM ID (launched 29-30 June 2026), with a pilot running 6-29 July 2026 and nationwide mass enrolment only starting 4 August 2026, so coverage under the new register is currently near zero and should be re-checked after Q3 2026.
